q: Which feature would let you distinguish a chloroplast from a mitochondrion in an electron micrograph?
options: A double membrane (envelope) enclosing the whole organelle, with a narrow space between
Stacks of flattened membrane sacs (grana) not joined to the inner membrane, plus starch grains
The presence of 70S ribosomes and loops of naked circular DNA within the inner fluid
A fluid-filled interior containing many dissolved enzymes, ribosomes and DNA
explanation: Both organelles have a double membrane, an enzyme-rich fluid interior (stroma/matrix), 70S ribosomes and naked circular DNA – evidence of their endosymbiotic origin. Only chloroplasts have thylakoids stacked into grana and starch grains, and they are usually larger; mitochondria have cristae formed by folding of the inner membrane.
